phase.preparation.title: Preparation
phase.preparation.description: Steps that can still be taken to ease the process for your family later.
phase.immediate.title: Immediate Actions
phase.immediate.description: These need attention within the first 24 hours.
phase.funeral_urgent.title: This Week
phase.funeral_urgent.description: Urgent matters for the first few days.
phase.notifications.title: Notifications & Claims
phase.notifications.description: Important notifications and benefit claims. You have more time for these.
phase.estate.title: Estate Settlement
phase.estate.description: Legal and financial steps over the coming months.
phase.special.title: Special Circumstances
phase.special.description: Additional steps that apply to your specific situation.
task.P0_1.title: Record Advance Directives
task.P0_1.description: Document end-of-life medical wishes and designate a trusted person (personne de confiance). This ensures your loved one's medical decisions are respected.
task.P0_1.deadline_note: Should be done while of sound mind
task.P0_1.where: Commission nationale de contrôle et d'évaluation, Omega 90, or the attending physician
task.P0_1.tips: The directive can be added to the shared electronic medical file (Dossier de Soins Partagé - DSP) for easy access by medical staff.
task.P0_2.title: Set Up Power of Attorney
task.P0_2.description: Appoint someone to manage personal welfare and financial affairs if cognitive capacity is lost. Important: standard bank mandates in Luxembourg automatically expire at the moment of death.
task.P0_2.deadline_note: Must be done before loss of capacity
task.P0_2.responsible: Your loved one, with a notary
task.P0_2.tips: Book a notary appointment soon - it can take a few weeks to get a slot.
task.P0_3.title: Prepare a Will
task.P0_3.description: Define how the estate should be distributed. Under Luxembourg law, children cannot be disinherited - they are 'forced heirs' with guaranteed shares (1 child: 50%, 2 children: 66%, 3+: 75%). Spouses are not forced heirs.
task.P0_3.deadline_note: Should be done before loss of capacity
task.P0_3.responsible: Your loved one, with a notary
task.P0_3.where: Any notary - they will register it with the Central Register of Wills at the AED
task.P0_3.tips: Even if a will exists, it's worth reviewing it with a notary to ensure it reflects current wishes and complies with Luxembourg's forced heirship rules.
task.P0_4.title: Pre-Plan the Funeral
task.P0_4.description: Choose burial or cremation and optionally pre-pay expenses. If cremation is desired, it's best to document this wish in writing. However, if no written proof exists, the closest family member can request cremation by declaring to the civil registrar.
task.P0_4.tips: Pre-planning avoids difficult decisions at a very hard time and ensures your loved one's wishes are respected.
task.1_1.title: Obtain Medical Certificate of Death
task.1_1.description: A doctor must officially pronounce the death. If cremation is planned, let the doctor know so they can issue the specific attestation needed.
task.1_1.responsible: Family (to call), or hospital/care home staff
task.1_1.where: Emergency services (112), on-call doctor, or hospital administration
task.1_1.tips: If at home, call 112 first. If in hospital or care home, the staff will handle this.
task.1_2.title: Contact a Funeral Home
task.1_2.description: A funeral director will transport the body, handle preparation, and can act as your proxy at the Commune for administrative formalities.
task.1_2.where: Private funeral homes - Erasmy, Welter, Beim Ruhl, or others
task.1_2.documents: Medical certificate, ID of deceased, clothes for the deceased
task.1_2.tips: The funeral home can help with many administrative steps. Don't hesitate to lean on them - this is what they do.
task.1_3.title: Register the Death at the Commune
task.1_3.description: Formally register the death to obtain Death Certificates (Actes de décès) and burial/cremation permits. Ask for 10-15 multilingual copies - you will need them for many subsequent steps.
task.1_3.responsible: Funeral home (on your behalf) or family
task.1_3.where: Civil Registry (Bureau de l'état civil) of the Commune where the death occurred
task.1_3.documents: Medical certificate, deceased's ID, Family booklet (Livret de famille) or marriage/birth certificates, your ID. For burial in a different commune: certificat de mise en bière. For cremation: add medical certificate of no violent death + pacemaker certificate.
task.1_3.tips: Go to the Commune where the death occurred, not where they lived. If death occurred at CHL in Luxembourg City, go to the Bierger-Center. You will also need to notify: schools of children/grandchildren (send them a copy of the death certificate), and if the deceased was a foreign national, their consulate or embassy (death certificate + international Form C + passport).
task.2_1.title: Arrange the Funeral or Cremation
task.2_1.description: The funeral or cremation must take place within a specific legal window and requires written authorisation from the civil registrar. Embalming is heavily restricted in Luxembourg. If cremation is chosen, ashes cannot be kept at home - they must be buried, placed in a columbarium, or scattered in designated areas.
task.2_1.where: Communal cemetery or the Crematorium of Luxembourg in Hamm
task.2_1.documents: Written burial/cremation authorisation from the civil registrar
task.2_1.tips: Both religious and non-religious (civil) ceremonies are possible - contact the communal administration where the burial will take place for options. Consider preparing a death notice (avis de décès / Todesanzeige) for the Luxemburger Wort, Tageblatt, or Contacto - the funeral home can usually arrange this, and the cost is reimbursable under the CNS funeral allowance. If you need more time than 72 hours, a special dispensation can be requested from the Ministry of Health's Médecin-inspecteur.
task.2_2.title: Notify Employers & Claim Bereavement Leave
task.2_2.description: Two things to do: (1) Notify the deceased's employer to stop salary. (2) Notify your own employer to claim paid bereavement leave. Both employees and apprentices are eligible.
task.2_2.deadline_note: Notify your HR on day 1 of your absence - this leave cannot be deferred
task.2_2.where: Your HR department and the deceased's employer
task.2_2.cost: Free - your normal salary continues during bereavement leave
task.2_2.tips: Luxembourg law provides: 5 days for a minor child, 3 days for a spouse/partner/parent/adult child, 1 day for siblings or grandparents. IMPORTANT: this leave cannot be deferred or compensated later. If the death occurs while you are on sick leave, the bereavement leave entitlement is lost. If it occurs during annual leave, the annual leave is interrupted and resumes after. If the death falls on a Sunday or public holiday, the leave carries over to the first working day. Your collective agreement may grant additional days beyond these legal minimums.
task.2_3.title: Notify Banks, Credit Cards & Investment Accounts
task.2_3.description: Inform all banks, credit card issuers, and investment/brokerage firms. Banks will immediately freeze accounts in the deceased's sole name to protect the estate. Joint accounts usually remain accessible to the surviving spouse. Ask each bank to cancel debit and credit cards in the deceased's name.
task.2_3.where: All banks (BCEE, BGL, POST, etc.), credit card issuers, investment accounts, and LuxTrust
task.2_3.lead_time: Accounts frozen instantly. Unblocking takes weeks and requires the Notary's Acte de Notoriété.
task.2_3.tips: Banks will usually pay the funeral bill directly from frozen funds if you hand them the original invoice. Keep the receipt. If the deceased had a safe deposit box (coffre-fort), it will be frozen too - accessing it requires the Acte de Notoriété from the notary (Step 4.1). Request final credit card statements to check for outstanding balances and recurring charges.
task.3_1.title: Claim CNS Funeral Allowance
task.3_1.description: The health fund pays a flat-rate lump sum to whoever advanced the funeral costs. Currently approximately €1,258 (indexed to cost of living). For children under 6, only 50% is paid; for stillbirths, 20%. The deceased must have been affiliated with a health insurance scheme.
task.3_1.deadline_note: You have up to 2 years, but sooner is better
task.3_1.responsible: The person who paid the funeral bill (any balance goes to spouse → children → parents → siblings if same household)
task.3_1.where: CNS (Caisse Nationale de Santé) - Service Remboursement
task.3_1.documents: Acte de décès, original paid funeral invoices, your bank details (RIB)
task.3_1.tips: Keep all original funeral receipts - you'll need them for this claim. If the death resulted from a work accident or occupational illness, an additional supplement (1/15 of annual compensation) may be available.
task.3_2.title: Apply for Survivor's Pension & Trimestre de Faveur
task.3_2.description: Apply for widow(er)'s/orphan's pension - this is not automatic. Also claim the 'Trimestre de faveur': the deceased's salary or pension continues for the month of death plus 3 additional months. Divorced former spouses are also eligible (proportional to marriage duration) if they have not remarried. The 1-year marriage/PACS rule has exceptions - see tips.
task.3_2.deadline_note: Apply as soon as possible to avoid income gaps
task.3_2.responsible: Surviving spouse/partner (>1 year registered), children, or divorced former spouse (if not remarried)
task.3_2.where: CNAP (Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Pension) for general-scheme pensions. Public-sector employees have a separate scheme. Deceased's employer for salary continuation.
task.3_2.documents: CNAP form, Acte de décès, marriage/PACS certificate (issued after death), bank account identification, school certificates for orphans
task.3_2.tips: CNAP will issue provisional payments while processing your application, so don't wait. The 1-year marriage rule does NOT apply if: the death resulted from a post-marriage accident, there is a child from the union, the age difference is less than 15 years, or the marriage lasted 10+ years. Cross-border: if the deceased was last affiliated in Luxembourg, apply directly to CNAP regardless of where you live - CNAP will coordinate with foreign pension bodies. Note: if you remarry or enter a new PACS, the pension stops (but a settlement equal to 5x or 3x the annual amount is paid depending on age). If the new union later dissolves, the pension can be reinstated.
task.3_3.title: Handle Housing, Utilities & Secure the Residence
task.3_3.description: Transfer or cancel the rental lease and all utilities. Secure the deceased’s home: consider changing locks, forwarding mail, and arranging care for pets or plants. If the deceased lived alone, the lease terminates automatically. If a spouse or child has lived there for over 6 months, the lease transfers to them.
task.3_3.deadline_note: No hard deadline, but act soon to stop billing and secure the home
task.3_3.where: Landlord, Enovos/Creos (energy), POST/Tango (telecom), Commune (water/trash), POST Luxembourg for mail forwarding (Réexpédition du courrier)
task.3_3.tips: Set up mail forwarding at POST Luxembourg to avoid missing important letters. Check for auto-renewing subscriptions - streaming services, gym memberships, loyalty programmes (Cactus, etc.). Track all expenses you personally incur securing the home - these can be reimbursed by the estate.
task.3_4.title: Claim Insurance Benefits
task.3_4.description: Contact insurers for: life insurance (Capital-décès), outstanding mortgage insurance (Assurance solde restant dû), and cancel health mutuelles (CMCM, DKV).
task.3_4.deadline_note: Check each policy - often 15-30 days to notify
task.3_4.where: Insurance providers (Foyer, Lalux, Baloise, AXA, etc.)
task.3_4.documents: Acte de décès, original policy, medical certificate of cause of death
task.3_4.tips: Locate all policies first. Check bank statements for premium payments if you're unsure which insurers are involved.
task.3_5.title: Notify Healthcare Providers
task.3_5.description: Inform the deceased's GP, dentist, specialists, physiotherapist, and pharmacy. This stops appointment reminders, cancels recurring prescriptions, and closes patient records. Some providers may have outstanding bills to settle.
task.3_5.where: The deceased's general practitioner (médecin traitant), dentist, specialists, physiotherapist, pharmacy
task.3_5.tips: CNS will automatically deregister the deceased after receiving the death certificate, but notifying individual providers avoids continued billing and unwanted appointment reminders. Check for any outstanding invoices or prescription plans that need cancelling.
task.4_1.title: Engage a Notary
task.4_1.description: A notary will identify all legal heirs, search the Central Wills Register, and issue an Acte de Notoriété (Certificate of Inheritance). This is required to unblock bank accounts and transfer property.
task.4_1.deadline_note: Start the process in month 1 or 2
task.4_1.documents: Acte de décès, family booklet, bank statements at date of death, property deeds
task.4_1.lead_time: 2-4 weeks to book a notary, then 1-3 months to receive the document
task.4_1.tips: Book early - notary appointments typically take 2-4 weeks to get. This step unlocks many others.
task.4_2.title: Decide: Accept or Renounce Inheritance
task.4_2.description: You have three options: (1) Accept simply, (2) Accept under benefit of inventory - this protects your personal assets if the deceased had unknown debts, (3) Renounce entirely. IMPORTANT: Be careful not to accidentally accept - managing, selling, or using ANY estate asset (e.g., selling the car, renting a property) is legally treated as tacit acceptance.
task.4_2.deadline_note: 3 months to make an inventory, plus 40 days to reflect
task.4_2.where: Tribunal d'arrondissement (District Court) - only needed for option 2 or 3
task.4_2.documents: Acte de décès, notary acts, ID
task.4_2.tips: If you suspect the deceased may have had debts, consider option 2 (accept under benefit of inventory). It protects you from inheriting liabilities beyond the estate's value. WARNING: Do NOT sell, manage, or use any estate assets before deciding - this counts as tacit acceptance and you lose the right to renounce.
task.4_3.title: File Succession Declaration & Pay Inheritance Tax
task.4_3.description: Submit the official tax return detailing the deceased's worldwide assets and liabilities. Tax rates depend on your relationship: 0% for children/spouse on legal shares, up to 36% for unrelated parties.
task.4_3.deadline_note: Within 6 months if death occurred in Luxembourg. Extended deadlines if death abroad: 8 months (Europe), 12 months (Americas), 24 months (Africa/Asia/Australia).
task.4_3.where: AED (Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA) - office of the deceased's last domicile in Luxembourg
task.4_3.documents: Declaration form, cadastral extract for property, proof of debts, IDs of declarants. If the deceased was married: certified copy of the marriage contract (if one exists).
task.4_3.cost: Depends on estate value and relationship to deceased. Declaration paper: min €2 stamp duty. Will search: €10 (electronic) or €20 (paper).
task.4_3.tips: Most notaries handle this on your behalf as part of the succession process. A notary is not legally required but is strongly recommended, especially for complex estates.
task.4_4.title: File Final Income Tax Return
task.4_4.description: For married couples, file a joint return for the full calendar year of death. The surviving spouse stays in the favourable tax class 2 for 3 years after the death, then moves to class 1A. For partners (PACS), joint taxation does NOT apply for the year of death - the surviving partner files individually.
task.4_4.deadline_note: By March 31 of the year following death
task.4_4.documents: Proof of income, Acte de décès. If receiving the trimestre de faveur, apply for a separate additional tax card from the RTS office.
task.4_4.tips: Good news for surviving spouses: you remain in tax class 2 for 3 years after the death. No action needed for this - it is applied automatically on your tax card.
task.4_5.title: Transfer Vehicle Registration
task.4_5.description: Transfer the vehicle title to an heir, or deregister it if selling.
task.4_5.deadline_note: Before driving the car long-term or selling it
task.4_5.documents: Acte de décès, notary certificate, car logbooks (Parts 1 & 2), valid MOT, valid insurance
task.4_5.tips: Make sure the MOT and insurance are both current before going to the SNCA.
task.4_6.title: Review & Update Your Own Documents
task.4_6.description: After losing a loved one, review your own legal and financial documents. If the deceased was named as a beneficiary, executor, guardian, or personne de confiance in any of your documents, those designations are now invalid and need updating.
task.4_6.deadline_note: No hard deadline, but don't put it off - an outdated beneficiary can cause problems
task.4_6.where: Your own notary (Chambre des Notaires), your bank, your insurance provider, CNAP
task.4_6.documents: Your existing will, insurance policies, pension nominations, power of attorney, advance directives
task.4_6.cost: Notary fees if amending a will (€150-€500); other updates are usually free
task.4_6.tips: Key things to check: (1) Your will - remove the deceased as beneficiary or executor. (2) Life insurance - update beneficiary. (3) Pension nomination - update at CNAP or employer. (4) Power of attorney - revoke if the deceased was your mandataire. (5) Advance directives - update personne de confiance. (6) Bank mandates. (7) Guardianship provisions for your children. If any of these still name the deceased, benefits may default to their estate rather than your intended recipient.
task.5_1.title: Handle Business Deregistration
task.5_1.description: Deregister or transition the business entity. The business permit (Autorisation d'établissement) becomes invalid but can be provisionally transferred to a spouse or descendant.
task.5_1.deadline_note: Notify CCSS within 8 days, Ministry of Economy within 1 month
task.5_1.where: CCSS, RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), Ministry of Economy
task.5_1.tips: If the family wants to continue the business, the business permit can be provisionally transferred. Act quickly on this.
task.5_2.title: Cross-Border Succession
task.5_2.description: If the deceased was a cross-border worker or foreign national, additional steps apply for international succession, pensions, and taxes.
task.5_2.where: Home country authorities and Luxembourg CNAP/AED
task.5_2.tips: Under EU rules (Brussels IV), succession follows the law of the country of habitual residence - unless the will explicitly chose another country's law. Surviving spouses of frontaliers apply for pension in their country of residence.
task.5_3.title: Manage Digital Accounts
task.5_3.description: Memorialize or close social media, email accounts, and cloud storage. Luxembourg has no specific law overriding tech company terms of service.
task.5_3.deadline_note: No legal deadline - take your time with this one
task.5_3.where: Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft - via their bereavement web portals
task.5_3.documents: Acte de décès, translated Acte de Notoriété, your ID
task.5_3.tips: Download necessary data BEFORE notifying platforms. Accounts are often permanently locked the moment you report the death.
